is there an entry test for UET Peshawar
responses: Admissions at UET Peshawar usually open after the intermediate results, through an online application on the university website. You need your matric and FSc marks, domicile, CNIC or B-Form, and photographs. Merit is based on your academic marks and the entry test score, and it changes every year by department.

For admission, apply online when admissions open, upload your documents, and check the merit lists on the UET Peshawar website. For Computer Systems Engineering the merit is usually high, so check the previous year's closing merit before applying.

what is the difference between CSE and software engineering
responses: BSc Computer Systems Engineering at UET Peshawar is an 8-semester degree. Core subjects include programming, data structures, digital logic design, computer architecture, operating systems, computer networks, databases, and embedded systems. In later semesters you can take electives like machine learning, computer vision, and artificial intelligence.
In CSE you study both hardware and software: C++ and Python programming, circuits and digital systems, networks, and operating systems. The degree takes 4 years, 8 semesters in total.

responses: Results are announced by the Examinations section and posted on the UET Peshawar student portal. Final exams are usually held at the end of each semester, and midterms are held in the middle of the semester. Check the academic calendar and the notice board for exact dates.

You can check your result on the student portal with your registration number. GPA is calculated from your grade points weighted by credit hours. If you fail a subject, you can usually repeat it in a later semester, and rechecking has a separate form and fee with a deadline.

responses: Yes, UET students can apply for merit scholarships, HEC need-based scholarships, and other government and private scholarships. Applications open through notices from the university, and you usually need your result card, fee receipt, income certificate, and CNIC.

responses: Start applying for internships in your 6th or 7th semester, or earlier if you have skills to show. UET departments and the career office share internship notices, and you can also apply directly to software houses, telecom companies, and research centers like NCBC.
For a first internship, build a simple one-page CV with your programming skills and 1-2 projects, and apply to several places. Practical experience matters more than a long CV.
